title: Speed to Lead: Why 5 Minutes Decides Who Books the Job
h1: Speed to Lead: Why 5 Minutes Wins the Job
meta: Respond to a lead in 5 minutes vs 30 and you're up to 100x more likely to connect (MIT Sloan 2026). 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first. The cheapest edge in the trades.
short: The cheapest advantage in the trades costs $0: answer fast. Respond in 5 minutes vs 30 and you're up to 100x more likely to connect, and 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first.
statLabel: More likely to connect responding in 5 minutes vs 30 (MIT Sloan 2026)

body.answer: Homeowners hire whoever they reach first.
body.html: 78% of homeowners hire the first business that responds (Lead Connect 2026). On shared leads especially, the homeowner is calling several pros — the fastest one books the job.

body.answer: The connection rate falls off a cliff after a few minutes.
body.html: Respond in 5 minutes instead of 30 and you're up to 100x more likely to connect (MIT Sloan 2026). Every minute of delay hands the job to a faster competitor.

body.h2: Never let a call die in voicemail
body.html: The average contractor misses ~14% of inbound calls (CallRail 2026). If you can't answer, auto-text back within seconds ('Sorry we missed you — what's going on?') and you save the job instead of funding a competitor's close.

faq.q: How fast should contractors respond to leads?
faq.a: Within 5 minutes. That's up to 100x more likely to connect than 30 minutes (MIT Sloan 2026), and 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first (Lead Connect 2026).

faq.q: Why do I lose leads I paid for?
faq.a: Usually speed. On shared leads the homeowner calls several pros and hires the first to respond. Slow response — or a missed call (~14% average, CallRail 2026) — hands the job to a competitor.

faq.q: What should I do if I can't answer a lead right away?
faq.a: Auto-text back instantly: 'Sorry we missed you — what's going on?' It keeps the conversation alive and saves the job while you get to the phone.
